OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 23, 2026 (11:05 a.m. EST)

STATUS: DIRECT DIVERSION CANAL FLOW NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Santee Cooper's operational feed says updated November 23, with latest daily elevations dated November 22. The operator reports daily figures rather than paired, individually time-stamped gauge readings. USGS Elloree (02169921) and Pinopolis (02172000) monitoring pages returned HTTP 403; the USGS instantaneous-values service could not be retrieved. Gauge vertical datums and observation-time comparability therefore remain unverified. Do not treat the nominal elevation difference as verified simultaneous hydraulic head.

LATEST OPERATOR DAILY ELEVATIONS (feet; datum/time comparability unconfirmed): November 22 — Lake Marion 74.09, Lake Moultrie 74.03, nominal Marion-minus-Moultrie +0.06 ft. November 21 — Marion 74.08, Moultrie 74.02, nominal +0.06 ft. Each lake rose 0.01 ft from November 21 to 22; the nominal difference was unchanged. November 23 elevations were not yet published on the checked feed. These are the latest available operator daily values, not direct canal measurements.

HYDRO OPERATIONS: Santee Cooper's November 23 feed tentatively schedules Jefferies Hydro on November 23 from 6 a.m. to 8 p.m., and November 24 from 6 p.m. to midnight. St. Stephen is listed as not scheduled on either day. These are tentative schedules, not confirmation of actual generation. The November 22 facility discharge table reports Jefferies 4,810, St. Stephen 0, Spillway Hydro 635 and Spilling 770 (units not independently confirmed here). None of these facility entries or schedules is a direct measurement of Diversion Canal flow.

INTERPRETATION — CONDITIONAL: If the operator's lake elevations are referenced to comparable datums and sufficiently close observation times, Marion being nominally 0.06 ft higher is consistent with a possible hydraulic tendency from Marion toward Moultrie. The small reported difference, uncertain comparability, wind setup, structures and operational variability prevent a defensible assessment of current direction or strength today. No canal velocity, discharge rate or measured current is claimed. Jefferies and St. Stephen operations do not by themselves prove Diversion Canal discharge.

SOURCES checked November 23, 2026: Santee Cooper operator feed (updated November 23; daily lake elevations and facility entries through November 22): https://azapp-lakespublic-prd-001.azurewebsites.net/ ; official lake data and gauge reference list: https://www.santeecooper.com/Community/Lakes/Lake-Data/ ; USGS Elloree https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02169921/ ; USGS Pinopolis https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172000/ . USGS primary gauge observations, datum reconciliation and direct canal-flow observations unavailable. Replaces November 22 commentary.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
temperature_analysis: WATER TEMPERATURE REPORT — Tuesday, November 24, 2026 (8:49 a.m. EST). Current primary USGS temperature observations could not be retrieved through either the instantaneous-values or latest-continuous data endpoints for stations 02171000 and 02172002. Current Celsius and Fahrenheit readings, observation timestamps, freshness and verified 24-hour changes are unavailable. This is a retrieval limitation, not confirmation of a station outage. Pineville measures bottom water at one Lake Marion location; Moncks Corner measures downstream tailrace canal water, not Lake Moultrie's surface. Neither represents lake-wide surface temperature. Seasonal cooling may influence baitfish distribution and blue catfish activity, but current fish locations, depths and feeding patterns cannot be inferred from unavailable temperature data. Consider forage, current, structure and on-water observations. Sources: https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02171000/ and https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172002/ .
